jobs.title: Founding / Principal Engineer, Trust & Control Infrastructure for AI Agents
jobs.description:
Stealth · San Francisco · Hybrid, 1–2 days a week in person to start · Q4 2026
Join the Founding Engineer Team at a founder-funded AI trust infrastructure company. Working prototype in review and test, development partners next, pre-seed/seed financing in progress, founder has gone founding-to-IPO before.

THE PROBLEM
Agents are being handed real authority. They approve refunds, move records between systems, change production configuration, and negotiate with other agents. Today no one can prove what an agent saw, what it decided, or what it did, and watching an agent is not the same as verifying it.
What an agent is shown decides what it does. That makes an agent's context and its decisions an attack surface nobody owns a control point over. Humans and systems need to constrain, correct, and sign off on agent decisions, before and after the fact, not just observe them. And none of this can depend on one framework or one model: a fleet built on LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, the OpenAI Agents SDK, the Anthropic Agent SDK, Google ADK, and MCP needs one independent standard underneath all of them.
We are building that standard: the way any agentic deployment, from a team's first ten agents to an enterprise's ten thousand, gains control over and insight into what its agents do, and puts them into production quickly, with trust and confidence.
How we do it stays under wraps until the development-partner phase. What it solves is above.

WHAT YOU WILL BUILD
• The framework integration layer. Our product running with at least two of the frameworks above, with identical guarantees, within your first quarter.
• The verification path. A design partner's security team can verify an agent's decisions end-to-end without us in the room.
• The control surface. How a human or a policy engine constrains, corrects, and signs off on an agent's decision, and how that holds when the agent is fast and the human is not.
• The performance envelope. Guarantees that cost agents milliseconds, not seconds. Measured, and published.
• The production stack. A working prototype exists and is in review and test. You review it, test it, and design the world-class production stack from it: your choices of languages, services, testing, agent tooling, and on-call become how we work.

WHAT YOU BRING
Background
• Six or more years building distributed systems or data infrastructure in production; you have owned a service other teams depended on. In the last two years part of that surface has been agentic: tool-calling models, agent runtimes, or MCP servers that other engineers' agents consume.
• Real time in at least one of: data infrastructure (databases, event streams, historians, ledgers), security or integrity engineering, observability, tracing, and audit systems, or developer platforms. Lineage from a company whose product was the record other systems trusted counts double; so does a team that shipped an agent product to real users and lived with what it did.
• Founding or pre-scale stage, or scaled a team from a handful to dozens, and you can say what you would do differently now that agents do a share of the engineering.

Systems experience (must have)
• You have built a system of record: an append-only, event-sourced, or ledger-style store where history is immutable, replay is deterministic, and people outside your team relied on it as the truth. You know what that guarantee costs, where it breaks, and what "deterministic" has to mean when a model is in the loop.
• Cryptographic integrity in practice: hashing, signing, content addressing, verification by a party who was not there. You designed for key rotation and algorithm change up front rather than bolting it on.
• Data lifecycle under constraint: deletion or retention designed into a system that also had to stay verifiable (regulatory erasure, legal hold, audit). You have lived the tension between "immutable" and "must be forgotten," including for what an agent was shown, not only what it wrote.
• A developer-facing surface you were accountable for: an SDK, library, API, or MCP server that other engineers, and their agents, build on, with versioning discipline, backward compatibility, and an upgrade path you owned.
• AI-native in production: a model or agent is a production component in something you shipped. You have written evals, handled non-determinism, built guardrails and human-in-the-loop approval paths, traced an agent's tool calls end to end, and dealt with prompt injection. Production experience with at least one of LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, the OpenAI Agents SDK, the Anthropic Agent SDK, Google ADK, or MCP.
• AI-native in practice: you build with coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or the like) writing, testing, and reviewing code under your direction, and you are judged on what ships, not on what you typed.
• Fluent in Python and TypeScript.

Strong signal
• Standards and protocol work: you have shipped against an evolving spec (MCP, A2A, OpenTelemetry's GenAI conventions, an IETF draft).
• Multi-tenant from day one: tenancy and permission boundaries for people and for the agents acting on their behalf.
• Shipped into a regulated or audited environment (finance, health, government, defense), built for an auditor who actually reads it.

The founding-era bar
• Moxie. You take the hard path when it is the right one, you ship under uncertainty with a small team, and you own the outcome, not the ticket.
• Intelligence. You reason from first principles, you write the design down before you prompt the agents, and you change your mind on evidence.
• Ambition. You want to set the standard an industry adopts, not fill a seat. If you would choose this over a lab offer, your three sentences should say why.
• Signal awareness. You know which three things on the board change the outcome this week and which twenty are noise, and you say so out loud, including when the founder has it wrong.
And you can be in San Francisco one to two days a week to start, with the rest remote: already in the Bay Area.

HOW WE WORK
• San Francisco, in person one to two days a week to start, remote the rest. The frameworks, the model labs, and most of the developers we are building for are within a few miles of each other here. Office location shared at the first call.
• AI-native by default. We use agents to build the thing that governs agents, and you are judged on what you ship.
• You would be one of the first three engineers. You work directly with the founder, a repeat enterprise-software operator who has scaled teams from founding stage through IPO and acquisitions, and with the founding engineer.
• Decisions in days, not quarters. Founder-funded through the prototype; pre-seed/seed financing in progress.
• Stealth now. A development-partner test phase precedes the public developer launch.

COMPENSATION
• Base salary: $190,000–$260,000. This is the pay scale we reasonably expect to pay for this position, set in good faith; where you land depends on demonstrated depth.
• Founding equity, sized to experience and scope. Four-year vest, one-year cliff, monthly thereafter.
• Benefits: medical, dental, and vision coverage; 401(k); flexible paid time off.

HOW WE HIRE
Step 1: a 30-minute conversation with the founder.
Step 2: a 60-minute technical deep dive on something you built that had to scale. Your choice.
Step 3: working together, or proceed. After the deep dive we decide together: a working session in San Francisco to meet and ideate on a real problem, with the prototype in front of you and under NDA, or, when the fit is already clear on both sides, straight to step 4.
Step 4: references, then offer. The process moves as fast as fit and mutual alignment allow.
A working-together path. This seat is critical and it is a partnership, so there is a second way in: begin by meeting and ideating with us before either of us commits to the full-time founding seat. Say in your application which path you want.

HOW TO APPLY
If you already know how you would build this, tell us. Send one artifact that shows scale design or models-in-the-loop work (a repo, a design doc, a postmortem, a talk), three sentences on why this problem, and your LinkedIn profile saved as a PDF (on your profile: More → Save to PDF), to opportunity@stealthaitrust.ai with the subject line "Founding Engineer — San Francisco". No cover letter.

NOTICES
Pay scale. The base salary range above is the pay scale for this position, provided consistent with California Labor Code § 432.3 as amended by SB 642 (effective January 1, 2026): a good-faith estimate of the salary range we reasonably expect to pay upon hire. Equity and benefits are in addition to base salary.
Salary history. Consistent with California Labor Code § 432.3, we will not ask about or rely on your salary history.
Fair chance. We will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records in a manner consistent with the California Fair Chance Act (Gov. Code § 12952) and the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance. We do not ask about criminal history before a conditional offer.
Equal opportunity. We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of any characteristic protected by federal, California, or San Francisco law.
Accommodation. If you need a reasonable accommodation at any point in the application or interview process, tell us and we will provide it.
Work authorization. You must be authorized to work in the United States. We can support transfers of existing H-1B, O-1, or TN status; we are not initiating new visa sponsorship at this time.

jobs.title: Full-stack Software Engineer III/Senior, AI Gateway
jobs.description:
About Ngrok Inc.

ngrok builds developer infrastructure to connect services and AI models, wherever they run.

Most developers know us as the way to put localhost on the internet. More than 15 million of them use ngrok, at companies like GitHub, Okta, HashiCorp, and Twilio. It's the same ngrok they've loved and leaned on for years, now with the power to run production traffic at scale.

Teams use ngrok to deliver APIs, connect to their customers' networks, manage device fleets, and route traffic between public and local AI models.

Across all of it, we hold ourselves to one standard: developers should be able to finish a whole job without becoming experts in every system it touches. We take on the complexity, make thoughtful choices by default, and keep developers in control of what matters to them.

A Few Things You Should Know

Our (unofficial) mascot is a shrimp. Yes, we make the puns.
We have a designated Chief Emoji Officer, and the role is vital to our success.
We like software that's serious and culture that's not.
Our competitive advantage is that we're having fun.

Still reading? Good. There's more below worth your time.

About The AI Gateway Team

Our AI Gateway team builds the systems that define how AI traffic is identified, controlled, and understood as it passes through ngrok.

We own the AI-specific control plane at the gateway layer: policies, usage tracking, and enforcement that sit directly on live customer traffic. Our systems must behave correctly under real-world conditions—traffic spikes, unexpected model behavior, misconfigured policies, and customers asking, “Why was this blocked?” or “Where did my tokens go?”

What You’ll Actually Do

Build and evolve the AI Gateway: You’ll work on the AI-aware gateway components that classify and handle AI traffic in real time. This code runs directly in the request path and must be fast, safe, and predictable.
Own AI traffic policy enforcement: You’ll design and implement AI Gateway Traffic Policy Objects—rate limits, usage caps, and access rules specific to AI workloads. These policies exist to prevent runaway costs, misuse, and accidental exposure without breaking legitimate traffic.
Track AI usage and token consumption: You’ll build and maintain systems that accurately measure AI usage—requests, tokens, and related metadata—so customers can understand how their AI systems behave and what they’re consuming.
Make AI behavior observable and explainable: You’ll expose clear, trustworthy signals around AI traffic: what was allowed or blocked, which policies applied, and how usage accumulated. When customers ask “what happened?”, the gateway should already know.
Design abstractions that hide complexity: You’ll work with product and design to build AI-specific gateway primitives that feel intentional and safe, without leaking provider quirks or infrastructure details into customer workflows.
Ship systems customers trust in production: You’ll collaborate closely with Gateway, Customer Data, and Platform teams to ensure AI usage data, policy enforcement, and billing signals line up—so customers can turn these features on with confidence.

You Might Be a Great Fit If…

You’re comfortable in a statically typed, compiled language such as Go, Rust, C++, or Java (with bonus points for Go)
Experience in frontend engineering, including expertise in TypeScript, React, HTML, CSS.
You’ve worked with AI/LLMs and can appreciate their unique brand of edge-cases
You care about developer experience and thoughtful abstractions
You enjoy defining system behavior, not just plumbing
You’ve thought about retries, limits, and costs before being asked
You like systems that move complexity from the user to the system

Extra Credit If You’ve Worked On

AI platforms or inference infrastructure
API gateways with product-level opinions
Usage limits, quotas, or billing-adjacent systems
Customer-facing observability tools

Tech Stack

ngrok runs entirely on AWS. Engineers develop by using remote development tools and/or ssh to connect to remote EC2 environments that run a full Kubernetes cluster of the ngrok stack, closely mirroring production. The codebase is primarily Go and TypeScript. We use Postgres for persistence, Kafka for streaming, Protobuf for service boundaries, and Kubernetes, Terraform, Helm, and Buildkite to operate and ship reliably. React is used for user interfaces, and GitHub supports our development workflows and remembers everything.

Location

This is a remote position for candidates outside of the Bay Area and a hybrid role for candidates within commuting distance to San Francisco. Our Bay Area employees commute to the office on Tuesdays and Wednesdays.

Sponsorship

All candidates must be US-based, and legally authorized to work in the United States.

At this time, ngrok is unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a permanent, ongoing basis without the need for current or future sponsorship.

Compensation

Senior Software Engineer

Tier 1 (SF, LA, Seattle, NYC): $202,500 – $247,500
Tier 2 (rest of US): $186,300 – $227,700

Software Engineer III

Tier 1 (SF, LA, Seattle, NYC): $180,000 – $220,000
Tier 2 (rest of US): $165,600 – $202,400

Job level and actual compensation will be evaluated based on factors including, but not limited to, qualifications objectively assessed during the interview process (including skills and prior relevant experience, potential impact, and scope of role), internal equity with other team members, market data, and specific work location. We provide an attractive mix of salary and equity.

Full Time Employee Benefits

Health stuff that actually matters. Full premiums covered on base healthcare, dental, and vision for you. Half covered for your dependents. Mental health and well-being support included, because taking care of your brain is as important as taking care of your teeth.
Retirement matching that doesn't suck. 401(k) with 100% match up to 3% of your salary and 50% match up to another 2%. Future you will appreciate present you.
Actually flexible time off. We say "open, flexible vacation policy" and actually mean it. Take the time you need. Your manager will bug you if you're not taking enough.
Parental leave that's realistic. Up to 16 weeks if you give birth, up to 8 weeks for new parents (birth, adoption, fostering—however your family grows).
Money to keep growing. Annual professional development budget for books, courses, conferences, or whatever helps you level up. Plus an annual home office/desk stipend to make your workspace not terrible.
Work from wherever. Co-working space stipend if you want to get out of your house but aren't near our SF office.
Lunch on us. 2x+ per week for employees onsite at our San Francisco office. Free food tastes better.
Company offsites. Twice a year we get the whole team together. It's part strategy, part bonding, part excuse to hang out with Bufo (the toad).
Regular feedback and fair compensation. Bi-annual reviews to make sure you're getting real feedback and staying competitively compensated. No surprises, no waiting around for performance conversations.

jobs.title: Oath Technologies  - Research Engineer, Tools & Infrastructure
jobs.description:
About Oath Technologies

Oath Technologies is a new research organization building tools for oversight of advanced AIs. As AIs become more powerful, it will become more difficult to understand and monitor their behavior. Oath is building oversight tools based on formal verification: rather than monitor AIs directly, humans define unambiguous rules, and AIs must provide trustworthy mathematical evidence of compliance. In this way, Oath will help keep humans safe and in control as AI advances.

Oath is a Focused Research Organization (FRO) incubated and fiscally sponsored by Convergent Research. Convergent has incubated 12 FROs spanning mathematics, astrophysics, neuroscience, climate, biology, and AI, including the Lean FRO (formal mathematics and verification) and E11 Bio (whole-brain circuit mapping). Oath is led by CEO Dr. Mike Dodds, and is based in Berkeley, CA.

Role Summary

Oath's research engineers will build novel formal methods tools and apply them at scale to AI oversight problems. To do this, we are hiring both formal methods specialists and engineers with skills such as developer tools, scalable testing, agent development, AI/ML, and others that complement Oath's mission. Engineers may have skills in one or several areas, and our team will be tightly integrated, with both categories working together.

Oath will target very difficult verification and oversight problems, far beyond previous formal verification projects in scale and complexity. Oath's research team will work iteratively, building tools, testing them on our flagship problems, identifying failures, and then feeding those back into our tool designs.

We plan to build an Oath team of around six people by the end of year one, growing to a steady state of around twelve people by year three. Oath's roadmap runs for five years, and we’ll set more ambitious targets as the outcomes of our work and changes in the profile of AI risk evolve. This is a strong fit for people who want to tackle complex, high-stakes challenges in a nimble, collaborative organization.

Oath's current plan is to build tools across three families: **design** (authoring new specifications), **lifting** (extracting specifications from existing systems that have none), and **audit** (stress-testing specifications for gaps or adversarial manipulation). We're applying these to a first flagship target, verified agent containment: proving that an AI agent can't escape the permissions and sandboxing meant to bound it, from the OCI container runtime down to Linux kernel isolation primitives. Most of this work will be done in Lean or adjacent formal-verification infrastructure, with AI agents doing much of the day-to-day drafting and proving under close review.

Primary Responsibilities

Contribute directly to Oath's research goals: building tools, applying them to real systems, and iterating based on what works.
Help scale Oath's tools to large, long-running experiments intended to map the frontiers of AI oversight capabilities.
Take deep ownership of problems, from framing the question, to overcoming obstacles, to delivering a working solution.
Collaborate closely with a small, high-context team, including significant use of AI agents as part of the day-to-day workflow.
Help set technical direction as the team and its workstreams grow, not just execute someone else's plan.
Document your work and reasoning so it doesn't stay trapped in one person's head.

Qualifications

Required:

Experience building tools engineers actually adopt: IDE integrations, language servers, CLI tooling, build-system integration.
Experience with AI-assisted developer workflows, agent scaffolding, or applied AI/ML engineering.
Comfort picking up formal methods concepts on the job, even without prior depth in the area.
Experience working in research and/or engineering teams delivering ambitious results.
An ability to learn quickly, build quickly, and pivot when necessary

Helpful, but not required:

Experience using coding agents or other AI tools for ambitious technical projects.
Knowledge of AI risks generally, and alignment with Oath's mission to counter AI risks.
A broad enthusiasm for deeply technical topics, and a passion for ideas.

Our Benefits Include:

Health, vision, and dental insurance
Generous time off + paid holidays
Company-paid life and AD&D, with voluntary supplemental options
Company 401(k) match up to 6%

We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse workplace where everyone has the opportunity to thrive. We believe in hiring individuals based on their unique talents—not on race, color, religion, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, age, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law or our company policies. We are more than a proud Equal Employment Opportunity employer. Our goal is to foster a healthy, safe, and respectful environment where all employees are valued and treated with dignity. Harassment of any kind is not tolerated here.

These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, ML API – AI Inference
jobs.description:
Cerebras Systems builds the world's largest AI chip, 56 times larger than GPUs. This architecture allows Cerebras to deliver industry-leading training and inference speeds; over 10 times faster than GPU-based hyperscale cloud inference services.

This order of magnitude increase in speed is transforming the user experience of AI applications, unlocking real-time iteration and increasing intelligence via additional agentic computation.

Cerebras works with the leading model labs, global enterprises, and cutting-edge AI-native startups. OpenAI recently announced a multi-year partnership with Cerebras, to deploy 750 megawatts of scale, transforming key workloads with ultra high-speed inference.

About The Role

Cerebras is building a new generation of disaggregated AI inference systems that combine GPU-accelerated prefill with ultra-fast decode on the Cerebras Wafer-Scale Engine.

We are hiring a Senior Software Engineer to build and evolve the ML API layer that makes this heterogeneous serving system accessible, reliable, and easy to use. You will own significant features and components across our inference APIs, model integration layer, and request-routing services, delivering a consistent experience across models and accelerator backends.

This role sits at the intersection of machine learning systems, API design, model serving, and distributed systems. You will translate evolving model capabilities and customer requirements into clear designs, lead implementation across multiple components, and carry features through validation, rollout, and production operation. Your work will help ensure that streaming, sampling, tool use, structured outputs, multimodal inputs, and model configuration behave correctly and consistently.

You will work closely with model enablement, compiler, runtime, cloud infrastructure, product, and customer-facing teams, as well as customers directly. This is a hands-on individual-contributor role with opportunities to lead small project teams, mentor engineers, and improve the quality and reliability of production inference software.

Responsibilities

Own features end to end. Design, implement, test, and operate features for chat completions, text generation, streaming, model configuration, tool calling, structured outputs, multimodal inputs, and emerging inference capabilities.
Lead multi-component delivery. Write clear design documents, evaluate technical tradeoffs, break projects into deliverable milestones, and coordinate implementation with a small group of engineers and partner teams.
Deliver consistent API behavior. Implement clear request and response semantics across GPU prefill, Cerebras decode, and other inference backends. Maintain compatibility with widely adopted inference interfaces and evolve owned APIs through validation, versioning, and deprecation best practices.
Enable new models and capabilities. Integrate foundation models, tokenizers, chat templates, generation configuration, sampling methods, and model-specific features into the serving platform.
Integrate serving components. Extend inference services and their integration with frameworks and runtimes such as vLLM, PyTorch, Hugging Face libraries, LLGuidance, and Cerebras runtime components.
Support disaggregated inference. Implement routing, state-transfer integration, error handling, retries, cancellation, and request lifecycle management to coordinate GPU prefill with Cerebras decode.
Deliver measurable performance improvements. Diagnose bottlenecks and improve time to first token, streaming latency, throughput, and resource efficiency through changes to tokenization, serialization, batching, scheduling, and communication.
Own correctness and release quality. Build conformance tests, model-validation suites, numerical comparisons, integration tests, and performance benchmarks that catch regressions in owned features and support safe releases.
Strengthen production reliability. Improve service metrics, tracing, logging, alerts, and diagnostic tools. Investigate production incidents, resolve root causes, and follow through on improvements to resilience and incident response.
Improve customer and developer experience. Partner with product, support, and solutions teams to understand user needs and make practical tradeoffs. Improve configuration, documentation, examples, and debugging workflows.
Raise the engineering quality bar. Provide thoughtful design and code reviews, mentor less-experienced engineers, share domain knowledge, and proactively remove delivery roadblocks.

5+ years of software engineering experience, including independent ownership of production services, distributed systems, or substantial software components.

Experience designing and delivering features that span multiple components, including documenting designs, evaluating tradeoffs, and coordinating implementation with other engineers.

Strong communication and collaboration skills, including experience leading technical delivery for a small project and supporting other engineers through reviews or mentorship.
Ability to turn ambiguous requirements into maintainable software while balancing customer needs, delivery timelines, and operational quality.

Preferred Qualifications

jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

Research Engineer, Synthetic Data

About The Role

As a Sr. Research Engineer on the Synth Data team at SpaceXAI, you’ll invent and scale the synthetic data that teaches our models new capabilities. You own the full loop: spotting a capability the model is missing, designing a data generation strategy, building reliable pipelines and verifiers, and validating that the resulting data actually moves the model.

You form hypotheses about what data will help, build the systems to produce it at scale, run ablations, and read the resulting traces and training signals to understand why it worked (or didn’t). Your datasets go directly into frontier training runs, and shape the development of Grok models.

What you’ll work on

Designing end-to-end synthetic data recipes that turn raw sources (traces, documents, codebases, workflows) into large, diverse, verifiable task sets.
Building strong verification and anti-hacking mechanisms so rewards are simple to compute and hard to game.
Controlling difficulty and diversity so data stays learnable and reflects real usage instead of collapsing into templates.
Running targeted ablations and analyses that demonstrate a dataset caused a capability improvement (and ruling out grader or data artifacts).
Iterating from traces and training results to close specific gaps, then turning successful one-off recipes into reusable infrastructure.
Partnering with research and other RL Data teams to translate model capability goals into concrete synthetic data plans.

You may be a fit if

You have research experience on synthetic or post-training data, in industry or academia. You've designed a data generation method, shipped the data into training, and can show its impact to the model you’re training.
You have strong software engineering fundamentals and have built non-trivial data pipelines, agent systems, or evaluation frameworks.
You have taste for what makes a good training task: hard enough to teach something real, simple enough to grade reliably, and resistant to reward hacking.
You are careful and systematic — understanding both aggregate metrics and close reading of raw outputs.
You enjoy turning messy, open-ended problems into repeatable, high-quality data production systems.

Applying

If there appears to be a fit, we'll reach out to schedule 2-3 short technicals. After, we'll schedule an onsite in our office, where you'll work on a small project, discuss ideas, and meet the team.

Samsara is seeking a high-impact, strategic seller to lead the go-to-market execution for our newest frontier: AI Products.  As an Enterprise Specialist (Overlay), you will partner with our Account Executives (AEs) to build deep partnerships with our largest, most complex accounts. You aren't just selling a tool; you are pioneering GTM, ensuring our customers realize continuous value from AI-driven automation.
About the Team:

This specialist team reports into a Sales Director (SD) and consists of specialist sellers aligned by segment and product.  AEs on the team are charged with accelerating the growth of a new product and will be incentivized on quarterly product sales targets mapped to 1 or more regional directors for mainline sellers in the segment.   Product Specialist sellers drive growth through strategic, high-value deal executing and enabling the segment overall to be successful.

Your efforts will result in real-world impact – helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.

.

jobs.description:
At Accenture Federal Services, nothing matters more than helping the US federal government make the nation stronger and safer and life better for people. Our 13,000+ people are united in a shared purpose to pursue the limitless potential of technology and ingenuity for clients across defense, national security, public safety, civilian, and military health organizations.

Join Accenture Federal Services, a technology company within global Accenture. Recognized as a Glassdoor Top 100 Best Place to Work, we offer a collaborative and caring community where you feel like you belong and are empowered to grow, learn and thrive through hands-on experience, certifications, industry training and more.

Join us to drive positive, lasting change that moves missions and the government forward!

Build AI that matters
. We ship production GenAI apps for confidential federal programs across defense, national security, public safety, civilian, and military health where reliability, privacy, and safety aren’t optional. AFS is a technology company within global Accenture and a Glassdoor Top 100 Best Place to Work. You’ll join a collaborative, inclusive community with hands-on growth, certifications, and industry training. We ship in weeks, not quarters, and measure success with latency, reliability, safety, and cost.

Confidentiality matters:
We don’t disclose program details publicly. If you advance, we’ll share specifics during the process.

Role Overview

You’ll turn mission needs into secure, reliable, and scalable GenAI applications no model training required. This is a hands-on role across agentic workflows, RAG, prompt/policy design, LLM evaluation, and platform integration. You’ll own the end-to-end path from use case evaluation → production deployment → operational excellence, partnering with product, security, data, and SRE to ship features safely and at scale.

What You’ll Do (Day To Day)

Design & ship mission grade GenAI: Build agentic workflows and RAG systems tailored to mission data and environments; target low hallucination, tight p95 latency, and predictable cost.
Agent frameworks & orchestration: Apply patterns from LangChain/LlamaIndex/Semantic Kernel; design task decomposition, tool use, guardrails, and recovery/fallback strategies.
Platform integration (no model training): Implement with AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, Amazon Kendra, and managed services (e.g., Document AI, Gemini, Gemma).

If you are passionate about solving real-world problems and ideating beside the best and the brightest, we invite you to join us!

This role is remote, but distance is no barrier to impact. Our hybrid teams collaborate across geographies to solve big problems, stay close to our customers, and grow together. You will be part of a culture that values trust, accountability, and shared success where your work truly matters.

Job Summary

The Technical Services Center of Excellence (CoE) builds the platforms, tooling and AI capabilities our engineers use to deliver security outcomes for customers. As Global Solutions Architect for AI Network Security, you will own the automation strategy for network security delivery. That spans traditional automation (scripting, API integrations, configuration management and workflow orchestration) as well as AI, which now plays a central role in the work. That includes assessing deployments, prescribing improvements, automating migrations, and providing conversational and agentic tools to consultants worldwide.

This is a full-stack role in the broadest sense. You are expected to be deeply fluent across the entire stack: frontend, backend, data, cloud infrastructure, CI/CD, networking and cybersecurity. You also need to understand how modern AI systems work and how they fail. You design zero trust into everything you build, you understand the threat landscape for LLMs and autonomous agents, and you know the controls that address it. You reason from first principles, ship to production, and raise the engineering standard of the people around you.

The role sits where business leadership, thought leadership and technical depth meet. You turn leadership priorities into technical direction, shape how the organization thinks about AI and security, and deliver working capabilities to our field teams in Customer Success and Professional Services. You report regularly to senior leadership within Technical Services, and you build the relationships across business units that let Technical Services execute more efficiently.

Your Impact

Own the Technical Services automation portfolio end to end: scripts, API integrations against PAN-OS, Strata Cloud Manager and Prisma APIs, configuration migration and validation tooling, and workflow orchestration. Choose deterministic automation or AI based on what the problem needs.
Architect and own production platforms that run maturity and security assessments across NGFW, Strata Cloud Manager, Prisma Access, Cloud-Delivered Security Services and Prisma SD-WAN.
Design assessment catalogs, parsers and evaluators with measurable accuracy: parser coverage, license-entitlement gating, and readiness reported as measured rather than rounded up.
Design and operate multi-agent AI systems on frontier models (for example Gemini and Claude on Vertex AI), including tool design, agent loops, structured outputs, retrieval, refusal handling and output-quality evaluation.
Apply zero trust principles end to end: identity-based, per-request access for users, services and AI agents; least-privilege, short-lived credentials; segmented workloads; encryption in transit and at rest; continuous verification and telemetry.
Secure AI systems by design. Threat-model agents and LLM features, defend against direct and indirect prompt injection, constrain agent autonomy and tool permissions, protect sensitive data in prompts, context and retrieval, and add guardrails and human approval where actions carry risk.
Build full-stack features in TypeScript, Python and React, with authorization, tenant isolation (row-level security), credential encryption and audit logging designed in from the start.
Operate CI/CD pipelines and Terraform-managed infrastructure on GKE across multiple regions, owning supply-chain controls, data residency, rollout safety, observability and incident follow-through.
Validate platform changes against live firewall, Prisma Access and SD-WAN lab environments before release.
Lead harness engineering for the Center of Excellence. Design and maintain the agent harnesses, skills, MCP servers, sub-agent roles, hooks, context files and quality gates that let engineers use coding agents (Claude Code or similar) safely and productively.
Make the Center of Excellence measurably more productive across its release schedule. Apply automation and AI to documentation, enablement content, service SKU development and launch readiness, so that new services and releases ship on time with complete supporting material.
Act as the bridge between business leadership and engineering: translate Technical Services priorities into architecture, roadmaps and delivered capabilities, and explain technical trade-offs in business terms.
Provide regular updates to senior leadership within Technical Services on progress, risks, automation ROI (hours saved, adoption, engagement outcomes) and AI spend.
Deliver tooling, enablement and reference architectures to field teams in Customer Success and Professional Services, and use their feedback to shape what gets built next.
Act as a thought leader on AI and network security: publish guidance, present at internal forums, and shape the practice's point of view on secure AI adoption.
Collaborate across business units, including Product, Engineering, Sales, Security and IT, and build relationships that remove friction and help Technical Services execute more efficiently.
Contribute to open-source SDKs for Palo Alto Networks APIs.
Mentor engineers, publish reference implementations, and hold regular office hours.

Required

Qualifications

8-12 years of professional software development experience. This includes at least one full-stack system you designed, shipped to production, and continued to own after launch.
Expert full-stack engineering across every layer: modern frontend frameworks (React or similar), backend APIs and services, relational data modeling and SQL, cloud infrastructure, containers and Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, and CI/CD. Working proficiency in TypeScript and Python.
Applied first-principles design: you can show a past architecture decision where you named the underlying constraint, chose what not to build, and justified the result.
Software design and testing discipline: clear interfaces, separation of concerns, dependency injection, and automated tests enforced in CI.
Strong cybersecurity foundation: application security (OWASP Top 10, secure coding, threat modeling), identity and access management (OAuth 2.0, OIDC, mTLS, RBAC), secrets and key management, and secure software supply chain practices (dependency pinning, SBOMs, provenance).
Zero trust architecture: you can explain and apply NIST SP 800-207 principles and the CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model pillars (identity, devices, networks, applications and workloads, data) to a real system you built or secured.
Network and security engineering: routing, segmentation, policy, VPN, SASE and threat prevention. You can deploy and test against a firewall, SASE or SD-WAN environment.
Early and advanced adopter of generative AI: you have worked hands-on with LLMs, agents, skills, MCP and coding agents since they emerged, and you can show how your practice evolved with them. Traditional automation depth: REST and XML APIs, scripting (Python, Bash), configuration-as-code, infrastructure as code, and workflow orchestration. You know when a deterministic script beats an AI agent, and you can explain why.
Advanced AI concepts: how LLMs behave, including context windows, tool calling, structured outputs, retrieval-augmented generation, embeddings, evaluation, and model limitations such as hallucination and non-determinism. Production experience on a major cloud (Google Cloud preferred: GKE, Cloud SQL, IAM, Secret Manager or KMS) and infrastructure as code (Terraform or OpenTofu).
Executive communication: you can present to senior leadership regularly, frame technical work in terms of business outcomes, and produce design documents and status reports that name risks, a critical path and a delivery forecast.
Cross-functional influence: a track record of building relationships and driving outcomes across business units and teams you do not manage, including with field teams such as Customer Success and Professional Services.
Comfortable working asynchronously with global teams across time zones.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Electrical or Computer Engineering, or a related technical field.

Preferred

Experience integrating AI security platforms such as Prisma AI Runtime Security (AIRS), or AI guardrail and red-teaming tooling.
Familiarity with Google SAIF, ISO/IEC 42001, or the NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile.
Experience with AI red teaming, LLM evaluation pipelines, or AI observability and tracing.
Experience with network automation tooling such as Ansible, Terraform providers for network devices, or pan-os-python and similar SDKs.
Experience with Google ADK, Claude Agent SDK, or authoring and publishing MCP servers, skills or plugins for others to use.
Experience producing technical documentation, enablement programs or service offerings (SKUs) in a professional services or customer success organization.
Experience with Bun, Hono, Zod, Drizzle or Vite.
Experience with Cortex or Cloud-Delivered Security Services.
Experience with multi-region architecture, data residency or cloud FinOps.
Security certifications such as CISSP, CCSP or OSCP.
Open-source maintainership or public SDK contributions.
Experience leading a small engineering team or practice, including onboarding and enablement.

Palo Alto Networks: PAN-OS and Panorama, Strata Cloud Manager, Prisma Access, Prisma SD-WAN, Advanced Threat Prevention, DNS Security, Advanced URL Filtering, WildFire, Enterprise DLP, Prisma AIRS, Cortex, Insights APIs.
AI: Gemini and Claude on Vertex AI, Google ADK, MCP, agent skills and plugins, an AI gateway.

Join the Founding Engineer Team at a founder-funded AI trust infrastructure company. Working prototype in review and test, development partners next, pre-seed/seed financing in progress, founder has gone founding-to-IPO before.

THE PROBLEM
Agents are being handed real authority. They approve refunds, move records between systems, change production configuration, and negotiate with other agents. Today no one can prove what an agent saw, what it decided, or what it did, and watching an agent is not the same as verifying it.
What an agent is shown decides what it does. That makes an agent's context and its decisions an attack surface nobody owns a control point over. Humans and systems need to constrain, correct, and sign off on agent decisions, before and after the fact, not just observe them. And none of this can depend on one framework or one model: a fleet built on LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, the OpenAI Agents SDK, the Anthropic Agent SDK, Google ADK, and MCP needs one independent standard underneath all of them.
We are building that standard: the way any agentic deployment, from a team's first ten agents to an enterprise's ten thousand, gains control over and insight into what its agents do, and puts them into production quickly, with trust and confidence.
How we do it stays under wraps until the development-partner phase. What it solves is above.

WHAT YOU WILL BUILD
• The framework integration layer. Our product running with at least two of the frameworks above, with identical guarantees, within your first quarter.
• The verification path. A design partner's security team can verify an agent's decisions end-to-end without us in the room.
• The control surface. How a human or a policy engine constrains, corrects, and signs off on an agent's decision, and how that holds when the agent is fast and the human is not.
• The performance envelope. Guarantees that cost agents milliseconds, not seconds. Measured, and published.
• The production stack. A working prototype exists and is in review and test. You review it, test it, and design the world-class production stack from it: your choices of languages, services, testing, agent tooling, and on-call become how we work.

WHAT YOU BRING
Background
• Six or more years building distributed systems or data infrastructure in production; you have owned a service other teams depended on. In the last two years part of that surface has been agentic: tool-calling models, agent runtimes, or MCP servers that other engineers' agents consume.
• Real time in at least one of: data infrastructure (databases, event streams, historians, ledgers), security or integrity engineering, observability, tracing, and audit systems, or developer platforms. Lineage from a company whose product was the record other systems trusted counts double; so does a team that shipped an agent product to real users and lived with what it did.
• Founding or pre-scale stage, or scaled a team from a handful to dozens, and you can say what you would do differently now that agents do a share of the engineering.

Systems experience (must have)
• You have built a system of record: an append-only, event-sourced, or ledger-style store where history is immutable, replay is deterministic, and people outside your team relied on it as the truth. You know what that guarantee costs, where it breaks, and what "deterministic" has to mean when a model is in the loop.
• Cryptographic integrity in practice: hashing, signing, content addressing, verification by a party who was not there. You designed for key rotation and algorithm change up front rather than bolting it on.
• Data lifecycle under constraint: deletion or retention designed into a system that also had to stay verifiable (regulatory erasure, legal hold, audit). You have lived the tension between "immutable" and "must be forgotten," including for what an agent was shown, not only what it wrote.
• A developer-facing surface you were accountable for: an SDK, library, API, or MCP server that other engineers, and their agents, build on, with versioning discipline, backward compatibility, and an upgrade path you owned.
• AI-native in production: a model or agent is a production component in something you shipped. You have written evals, handled non-determinism, built guardrails and human-in-the-loop approval paths, traced an agent's tool calls end to end, and dealt with prompt injection. Production experience with at least one of LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, the OpenAI Agents SDK, the Anthropic Agent SDK, Google ADK, or MCP.
• AI-native in practice: you build with coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or the like) writing, testing, and reviewing code under your direction, and you are judged on what ships, not on what you typed.
• Fluent in Python and TypeScript.

Strong signal
• Standards and protocol work: you have shipped against an evolving spec (MCP, A2A, OpenTelemetry's GenAI conventions, an IETF draft).
• Multi-tenant from day one: tenancy and permission boundaries for people and for the agents acting on their behalf.
• Shipped into a regulated or audited environment (finance, health, government, defense), built for an auditor who actually reads it.

The founding-era bar
• Moxie. You take the hard path when it is the right one, you ship under uncertainty with a small team, and you own the outcome, not the ticket.
• Intelligence. You reason from first principles, you write the design down before you prompt the agents, and you change your mind on evidence.

And you can be in San Francisco one to two days a week to start, with the rest remote: already in the Bay Area.

HOW WE WORK

• AI-native by default. We use agents to build the thing that governs agents, and you are judged on what you ship.

Job Description

Teach AI how business actually works

AI agents are starting to take on real business work: releasing blocked invoices, re-planning supply, preparing the financial close. To do it safely, they need more than access to data. They need to know what an order, a supplier and a cost center are, how they connect, which rules and authorizations apply, and what happened the last time someone made a similar decision. When executing mission-critical business processes, an answer or action that is right 90% of the time is not good enough.

SAP systems hold the context for many of the world's largest companies. SAP's knowledge graph for SAP S/4HANA alone is based on 452,000 tables, 80,000 CDS views (semantic data models) and 7.3 million fields. Yet much of the meaning, especially in each company's own extensions, configuration and decision history, is still implicit. A 'customer' in sales, a 'business partner' in finance and an 'account' in CRM can be the same company described three ways, and an agent deciding whether to raise a credit limit has to know that. This is not a data-cleaning problem, it is a knowledge-representation problem. Today that context, the semantic layer agents rely on, is mostly modeled by hand, one company at a time. We think it can be learned, so AI agents can act on business data, not just read it. SAP's Autonomous Enterprise depends on that, and it is what makes the agents people work with in Joule Work, SAP’s AI workspace, accurate enough to trust.

As a Senior Data Scientist, you'll own a research thread end to end: from an open question, to a method and a benchmark, to a prototype a product team adopts. This is a research and modeling role, not product analytics.

SAP Research & Innovation North America

We are a team of scientists and engineers at SAP Labs in Palo Alto, minutes from Stanford. We look a few years ahead and scout emerging technologies, take the early, riskier bets that product teams can’t always take, and prove or drop them fast. SAP’s product teams build and run SAP Knowledge Graph, we look beyond and find and prove methods that demonstrate improvement or paradigm shifts. Our job is to spot the opportunities that will matter most to SAP and our customers, and to get there early. We prototype with dedicated GPU compute on realistic business data and, in co-innovation projects, on real data for training and evaluating models. We publish research, work with startups, universities and institutes including Stanford HAI and UC Irvine, and hand what works to SAP's product teams. We move like a small lab, with the reach of a company whose software runs finance, supply chain and HR for many of the world's largest companies.

What You Will Work On

Research you own. Take an open question from ambiguous framing to a reproducible result, and decide what to do next based on what you find. Closely collaborate with top universities and institutes such as Stanford HAI.
What comes next. Reproduce promising new papers on SAP data within weeks and recommend which deserve a bigger bet.
Better ways to build the semantic layer agents need. New methods to learn and maintain ontologies of business objects, processes, rules and actions, with SAP's semantic models as the backbone and LLMs, schema matching and entity resolution to extend them.
Agents grounded in business context. Graph-augmented retrieval and text-to-query agents (SQL, SPARQL, APIs) over very large schemas, with checks against business rules and access rights, and governed actions.
Models that learn from relational data. Graph neural networks and relational foundation models, such as SAP-RPT-1.6, applied with knowledge-graph context to prediction, anomaly detection and what-if analysis.
Honest measurement. Datasets, benchmarks and evaluation harnesses that show whether an approach works on realistic enterprise data, and why, using synthetic or privacy-preserving data where real data can't be shared.
Work others can use. Clean Python that others build on, prototypes built together with (and adopted by) product and engineering teams, published research papers or open-source releases, and mentoring for interns.

In Your First Year, Success Could Look Like

Own one research thread end to end, hands on. For example, schema linking for agents over SAP finance data, taken from baseline to benchmark to a prototype a product team adopts.
A paper submission or open-source release.

This is a senior individual-contributor role, comparable to Senior Research or Data Scientist at other Bay Area technology companies.

Qualifications

Required

Typically 5+ years of hands-on data science, machine learning or applied research, or a PhD plus 2+ years, taking projects from an open question to a measurable result. An MS or PhD in computer science, machine learning, statistics, mathematics or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Hands-on depth in at least one of the following, and an appetite to learn the others:
Knowledge graphs, ontologies or semantic layers: RDF, OWL, SHACL, SPARQL, or property graphs with Cypher or similar
Entity resolution, schema matching or data integration
Machine learning on relational, graph or tabular data, including GNNs
LLM systems over structured data: text-to-SQL, schema linking and API discovery, GraphRAG, agents, evaluation

Solid foundations in machine learning and statistics, with disciplined experimentation: strong baselines, ablations, leakage-safe splits, error analysis and honest reporting of what didn't work.
Strong Python and SQL, and PyTorch or a similar framework; at ease with large, messy, multi-table data.
Strong problem solving skills, shown by concrete examples: you have turned a vague question into an experiment that gave a clear answer within weeks.
Strong communication skills, shown by concrete examples: you have written up a negative or mixed result clearly enough that others acted on it, and you can explain your work concisely verbally and on a one pager to a scientist or executive.

Preferred

Publications at venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, KDD, ACL/EMNLP, SIGMOD/VLDB, ISWC, WWW, or contributions to open-source projects.
Graph databases, vector search, or large-scale data processing such as Spark.

Process mining, causal inference or forecasting, and familiarity with enterprise processes such as finance, procurement or supply chain.

Job Description

Teach AI how business actually works

AI agents are starting to take on real business work: releasing blocked invoices, re-planning supply, preparing the financial close. To do it safely, they need more than access to data. They need to know what an order, a supplier and a cost center are, how they connect, which rules and authorizations apply, and what happened the last time someone made a similar decision. When executing mission-critical business processes, an answer or action that is right 90% of the time is not good enough.

SAP systems hold the context for many of the world's largest companies. SAP's knowledge graph for SAP S/4HANA alone is based on 452,000 tables, 80,000 CDS views (semantic data models) and 7.3 million fields. Yet much of the meaning, especially in each company's own extensions, configuration and decision history, is still implicit. A 'customer' in sales, a 'business partner' in finance and an 'account' in CRM can be the same company described three ways, and an agent deciding whether to raise a credit limit has to know that. This is not a data-cleaning problem, it is a knowledge-representation problem. Today that context, the semantic layer agents rely on, is mostly modeled by hand, one company at a time. We think it can be learned, so AI agents can act on business data, not just read it. SAP's Autonomous Enterprise depends on that, and it is what makes the agents people work with in Joule Work, SAP's AI workspace, accurate enough to trust.

As Principal Data Scientist, you will define and lead our research toward that goal and work with product teams to ship the results. This is a research and modeling role, not product analytics.

SAP Research & Innovation North America

We are a team of scientists and engineers at SAP Labs in Palo Alto, minutes from Stanford. We look a few years ahead and scout emerging technologies, take the early, riskier bets that product teams can’t always take, and prove or drop them fast. SAP's product teams build and run SAP Knowledge Graph, we look beyond and find and prove methods that demonstrate improvement or paradigm shifts. Our job is to spot the opportunities that will matter most to SAP and our customers, and to get there early. We prototype with dedicated GPU compute on realistic business data and, in co-innovation projects, on real data for training and evaluating models. We publish research, work with startups, universities and institutes including Stanford HAI and UC Irvine, and hand what works to SAP's product teams. We move like a small lab, with the reach of a company whose software runs finance, supply chain and HR for many of the world's largest companies.

What You Will Work On

A research agenda with a point of view. Pick the two or three bets where SAP can lead in AI on business data, agree up front how we will know each one is working, and stop the ones that aren't. Closely collaborate with top universities and institutes such as Stanford HAI.
What comes next. Track emerging research, such as relational and graph foundation models, neuro-symbolic agents and context graphs, test it on SAP data before the market settles, and make the case for the next bet.
Business semantics that can be learned. New methods to learn, align and evolve ontologies and knowledge graphs of business objects, rules and actions from SAP metadata, master data, documents and process data, combining LLM-assisted ontology learning, schema matching and entity resolution with targeted expert review.
Agents grounded in business semantics. Graph-grounded retrieval; semantic parsing into SQL, SPARQL and OData calls, including finding the right API, across very large schemas; and governed actions: checks that an agent's plan respects business rules and the user's authorizations before it runs.
Models that combine structure and statistics. Graph learning and relational foundation models (such as SAP-RPT-1.6), using knowledge-graph structure to predict, explain and simulate business outcomes.
The yardstick. Benchmarks and simulation environments for agents on ERP data, where today's public benchmarks fall short, so SAP knows when AI is accurate and reliable enough to act on.
Results that land. Work directly with data teams and domain experts in co-innovation projects, turning messy enterprise data problems into tractable ontology problems, and work with the teams behind SAP Knowledge Graph, SAP Business Data Cloud and Joule, SAP's AI assistant, to ship what works.
A stronger research community. Publish at top venues, release code and benchmarks where we can, co-lead university collaborations, and mentor scientists and PhD interns.

Papers submitted, and a benchmark or open-source release others use
Scientists doing better work because of you

Typically 8+ years in applied research, data science or machine learning, or a PhD and 5+ years, including research you led that changed a product or platform. An MS or PhD in computer science, machine learning, statistics, mathematics or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Publications at venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, KDD, ACL/EMNLP, SIGMOD/VLDB, ISWC, WWW, or widely used open-source software, datasets or semantic standards work.

Job Summary

The Technical Services Center of Excellence (CoE) builds the platforms, tooling and AI capabilities our engineers use to deliver security outcomes for customers. As Global Solutions Architect for AI Network Security, you will own the automation strategy for network security delivery. That spans traditional automation (scripting, API integrations, configuration management and workflow orchestration) as well as AI, which now plays a central role in the work. That includes assessing deployments, prescribing improvements, automating migrations, and providing conversational and agentic tools to consultants worldwide.

This is a full-stack role in the broadest sense. You are expected to be deeply fluent across the entire stack: frontend, backend, data, cloud infrastructure, CI/CD, networking and cybersecurity. You also need to understand how modern AI systems work and how they fail. You design zero trust into everything you build, you understand the threat landscape for LLMs and autonomous agents, and you know the controls that address it. You reason from first principles, ship to production, and raise the engineering standard of the people around you.

The role sits where business leadership, thought leadership and technical depth meet. You turn leadership priorities into technical direction, shape how the organization thinks about AI and security, and deliver working capabilities to our field teams in Customer Success and Professional Services. You report regularly to senior leadership within Technical Services, and you build the relationships across business units that let Technical Services execute more efficiently.

Your Impact

Own the Technical Services automation portfolio end to end: scripts, API integrations against PAN-OS, Strata Cloud Manager and Prisma APIs, configuration migration and validation tooling, and workflow orchestration. Choose deterministic automation or AI based on what the problem needs.
Architect and own production platforms that run maturity and security assessments across NGFW, Strata Cloud Manager, Prisma Access, Cloud-Delivered Security Services and Prisma SD-WAN.
Design assessment catalogs, parsers and evaluators with measurable accuracy: parser coverage, license-entitlement gating, and readiness reported as measured rather than rounded up.
Design and operate multi-agent AI systems on frontier models (for example Gemini and Claude on Vertex AI), including tool design, agent loops, structured outputs, retrieval, refusal handling and output-quality evaluation.
Apply zero trust principles end to end: identity-based, per-request access for users, services and AI agents; least-privilege, short-lived credentials; segmented workloads; encryption in transit and at rest; continuous verification and telemetry.
Secure AI systems by design. Threat-model agents and LLM features, defend against direct and indirect prompt injection, constrain agent autonomy and tool permissions, protect sensitive data in prompts, context and retrieval, and add guardrails and human approval where actions carry risk.
Build full-stack features in TypeScript, Python and React, with authorization, tenant isolation (row-level security), credential encryption and audit logging designed in from the start.
Operate CI/CD pipelines and Terraform-managed infrastructure on GKE across multiple regions, owning supply-chain controls, data residency, rollout safety, observability and incident follow-through.
Validate platform changes against live firewall, Prisma Access and SD-WAN lab environments before release.
Lead harness engineering for the Center of Excellence. Design and maintain the agent harnesses, skills, MCP servers, sub-agent roles, hooks, context files and quality gates that let engineers use coding agents (Claude Code or similar) safely and productively.
Make the Center of Excellence measurably more productive across its release schedule. Apply automation and AI to documentation, enablement content, service SKU development and launch readiness, so that new services and releases ship on time with complete supporting material.
Act as the bridge between business leadership and engineering: translate Technical Services priorities into architecture, roadmaps and delivered capabilities, and explain technical trade-offs in business terms.
Provide regular updates to senior leadership within Technical Services on progress, risks, automation ROI (hours saved, adoption, engagement outcomes) and AI spend.
Deliver tooling, enablement and reference architectures to field teams in Customer Success and Professional Services, and use their feedback to shape what gets built next.
Act as a thought leader on AI and network security: publish guidance, present at internal forums, and shape the practice's point of view on secure AI adoption.
Collaborate across business units, including Product, Engineering, Sales, Security and IT, and build relationships that remove friction and help Technical Services execute more efficiently.
Contribute to open-source SDKs for Palo Alto Networks APIs.
Mentor engineers, publish reference implementations, and hold regular office hours.

Required

Qualifications

8-12 years of professional software development experience. This includes at least one full-stack system you designed, shipped to production, and continued to own after launch.
Expert full-stack engineering across every layer: modern frontend frameworks (React or similar), backend APIs and services, relational data modeling and SQL, cloud infrastructure, containers and Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, and CI/CD. Working proficiency in TypeScript and Python.
Applied first-principles design: you can show a past architecture decision where you named the underlying constraint, chose what not to build, and justified the result.
Software design and testing discipline: clear interfaces, separation of concerns, dependency injection, and automated tests enforced in CI.
Strong cybersecurity foundation: application security (OWASP Top 10, secure coding, threat modeling), identity and access management (OAuth 2.0, OIDC, mTLS, RBAC), secrets and key management, and secure software supply chain practices (dependency pinning, SBOMs, provenance).
Zero trust architecture: you can explain and apply NIST SP 800-207 principles and the CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model pillars (identity, devices, networks, applications and workloads, data) to a real system you built or secured.
Network and security engineering: routing, segmentation, policy, VPN, SASE and threat prevention. You can deploy and test against a firewall, SASE or SD-WAN environment.
Early and advanced adopter of generative AI: you have worked hands-on with LLMs, agents, skills, MCP and coding agents since they emerged, and you can show how your practice evolved with them. You use Claude Code or a similar agent harness at an advanced level every day, including multi-agent workflows, custom skills, hooks, sub-agents and MCP integrations.
Harness engineering: a deep understanding of how to engineer the environment around a model. Traditional automation depth: REST and XML APIs, scripting (Python, Bash), configuration-as-code, infrastructure as code, and workflow orchestration. You know when a deterministic script beats an AI agent, and you can explain why.
Advanced AI concepts: how LLMs behave, including context windows, tool calling, structured outputs, retrieval-augmented generation, embeddings, evaluation, and model limitations such as hallucination and non-determinism. You have built and operated at least one LLM-backed application with tool-using agents in production: you designed the tools, implemented the agent loop, and evaluated output quality.
